images.title: Zero counts, a missed match does not
images.purpose: Show that a score of 0 is a real value that counts, while a match not played is left out of both the total and the count.
images.composition: One row of 7 match boxes across the centre, one box greyed and struck out, with a short count caption and a single result line below.
exact_structure: A row of 7 equal square boxes, left to right: 57, 13, 0, 84, Did not play, 51, 27.
The boxes 57, 13, 84, 51 and 27 are teal (#0072B2) outlined.
The 0 box is green (#009E73) with a small green tick above it.
The Did not play box is grey (#6B7280) with a grey diagonal line struck through it.
Under each of the 6 counted boxes (all except the struck box) sits a small green dot; there is no dot under the struck box. Centred below the row, the caption reads 6 matches played.
Below that caption the result line reads 232 ÷ 6 ≈ 38.67.
rejection: a green dot under the Did not play box
a number of boxes other than 7
images.takeaway: A zero score counts in the mean; a match not played is not a value and is left out.
images.description: Seven match boxes 57, 13, 0, 84, did not play, 51, 27, with the 0 ticked, the missed match struck out and 232 ÷ 6 ≈ 38.67 below.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Ask why the 0 box keeps its tick while the grey box is struck out, before dividing.

image_decisions.why: The difference between 0 and no value is easiest to see when the two boxes sit side by side.
